I will keep the full 10.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because I have well irrigation, this system fits Quzhou County, and it is still the safest way for me to hold grain yield on a small farm. I will put more water and management into winter wheat because spring here is dry and wheat depends more on irrigation, while summer maize can use the rainy season and usually needs less water. For seed, I will use better seed rather than traditional seed, because on my land I care more about stable yield than saving a little on seed cost. For fertilizer, I will stay in a moderate range instead of chasing the very highest input, because my farm is not large, some family labor is away from home, and I want a balance of yield, cost, and work. I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it is practical for returning residue and preparing the seedbed, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest because that saves time and matches the local double-cropping rhythm. I will spray only as needed but I still plan regular disease, weed, and insect control so I do not lose yield at key stages.
